catalogue_requests.summary: Read the M1 mirror photocurrent channels the ophyd electrometer publishes, without staging or triggering it.
catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class reads a named electrometer channel set of an ophyd device; cap.sensing.read.v1 has an open values object. The reviewed read-only subset uses an x-cap id with an inline output schema meanwhile.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend only: `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/nsls-ii-ari__ari_sxn_common --backend fake` exited 0 and printed the digest above. The evidence state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level or a hardware run. The package is model-authored (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, model_id deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run_id helper-wave-1-020) and reviewed_by is null; no human reviewed or tested it, and no hardware or EPICS IOC was attached. No upstream code was imported or run while authoring.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes the config-only OphydDriver helper with ari_sxn_common.ari_ophyd:M1 as the entry class. M1 is an ophyd Device, but every served member is a nested custom Device or custom motor: the five mirror axes are Component(ID29EpicsMotor, ...) at src/ari_sxn_common/ari_ophyd.py:97-106, ID29EpicsMotor is an EpicsMotor subclass at src/ari_sxn_common/common_ophyd.py:116, the vacuum child is _VacuumDevices/_AriSxnC at ari_ophyd.py:9-35, slits is BaffleSlit and diag is Diagnostic at ari_ophyd.py:112-140. The Ophyd source proof accepts only direct Component(EpicsSignal | EpicsSignalRO | Signal, literal) declarations of the selected class, so OphydDriver cannot bind this interface without inventing a declaration. The package is a direct Driver over the confirmed entry symbol M1 (ari_ophyd.py:38), with a native.py factory. The other card entry symbols were confirmed too: BaffleSlit at common_ophyd.py:691 and Diagnostic at common_ophyd.py:595, and both are used as children of M1.

Covered: 22 numeric telemetry reads (five mirror-axis readbacks, four baffle-slit blade readbacks, two diagnostic blade/filter readbacks, four diagnostic current means, four baffle-slit current means and three vacuum gauge signals), the parent locations read, and one extension action that calls the upstream M1.trigger(). Every numeric read is a fresh native Signal call with use_monitor=False on the motor readback, gauge or mean_value signal; locations.get() runs the upstream LocationSignal.get. The trigger action reports issued=true and waited=false: it calls M1.trigger(), which itself triggers the slits and diagnostic children, but does not await the returned native Status and does not claim acquisition completion.

NOT COVERED: motor or slit setpoint writes and all motion, LocationSignal.set, homing, the gv shutter state, the diagnostic camera image/array_data and any camera artifact, and trigger completion. The card lists no write and the clone states no travel bound, so no write limit can be sourced; adding motion would need an operator envelope and a source-backed stop path. The camera image is not retrieved by this read-only section driver even though M1.trigger internally triggers the camera; this package does not claim image capture. The parent M1 locations signal is empty unless the deployment passes locations_data at construction; the native factory accepts that option and the fake uses placeholder location names.

Units and limits: the clone states no engineering unit for any motor, current or vacuum record, so no field declares a unit. The package declares no Limit because it has no numeric input; the trigger action has no input. The locations array length is deployment configuration, not a fixed device bound. No site-limits.example.json is provided because there is no bounded input to narrow.

Safety: risk is R0 because this package exposes only reads and the section trigger; it exposes no motor, slit, shutter or other physical motion command. The runtime e-stop is a software latch only; no estop_physical_ref or safe_state action is declared, and no physical stop is claimed. The upstream section does contain motors, but this package does not command them; a future motion package would need a source-backed stop and an operator travel envelope.

Mock path: the card prefers a fake. The fake is a source-shaped in-memory stand-in (F0), not a recording and not the upstream simulator; it holds the same public child names and Signal-shaped get/use_monitor calls, and its trigger returns a completed fake Status. All fake numbers and location names are placeholders marked in fake.py, not facts, limits or deployment defaults. The fake imports no ophyd, epics, nslsii or upstream code.

Hardware backend: .native:connect constructs the upstream M1 class under an operator-given prefix and name, passes optional locations_data, and waits once for connection with the operator timeout. It has never been imported or run. Deployment validation is required for the M1 PV prefix, the literal ARI_M1: prefix in the vacuum child (ari_ophyd.py:34), the parent locations_data mapping, every PV named by the connected Components (including the diagnostic camera and gv shutter that this package does not read), and the upstream import layout. The pinned ari_ophyd.py imports common_ophyd as a top-level module (ari_ophyd.py:1); native.py first tries the installed import and, only when that fails on common_ophyd, adds the package directory to sys.path for the import. This fallback changes no upstream file and must be validated in the deployment environment.

Gate warning: G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected and is the only warning. SAFE-014 has no limit to probe because the driver declares no limit on an actuating capability; every other CL3 conformance test passed. G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings, and the clone remained unmodified.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation (the OphydDriver proof refuses M1's nested Devices, as the readiness evidence said), every read and fact against ari_ophyd.py and common_ophyd.py, and the only capability. The read-only R0 subset is honest (fresh get(use_monitor=False) of motor readbacks, currents and gauges; no motion), but the capability called M1.trigger(), whose children are ID29EM (an ophyd NSLS_EM) and a Prosilica with ophyd's SingleTrigger (common_ophyd.py:180, 245, 673-688, 763-771): classic ophyd refuses to trigger an unstaged detector and the package never stages, while the fake's trigger always returned a done status. The reviewer replaced it with the observation x-cap.nsls-ii-ari.m1_photocurrent.v1 (verb read, a fresh get of diag.currents.current1.mean_value, which M1 exposes as photocurrent, ari_ophyd.py:86-94), rewrote safe_state and the docstring and added six facts (driver.py, facts.md), removed the trigger stand-ins (fake.py), replaced the trigger cases (test_driver.py), updated the native.py docstring and regenerated reference.json and REFERENCE.md; gate and strict collector pass with G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, digest unchanged (sha256:0bd9a2381b9093e647d8e95412fe1206cb962f026a6322c357ea87304f0554a7). RESULT.json's catalogue request for x-cap.nsls-ii-ari.m1_trigger.v1 is superseded. For the human reviewer: Read-only view of a motorised mirror section (five mirror motors, four slit blades, diagnostic blade and filter); motion, the gv shutter and the camera are not covered and no stop is declared. Constructing M1 writes 'EM180' into eight electrometer plugin nd_array_port PVs (common_ophyd.py:212-224), and native.py puts the installed package directory on sys.path for the upstream's top-level 'common_ophyd' import; the vacuum child's 'ARI_M1:' prefix is hard-coded upstream (ari_ophyd.py:34). The photocurrent is the plugin's last computed mean, stale while the electrometer is not acquiring.
